cards.f: Principal source of energy for biological systems
cards.b: The Sun. Producers transfer light energy into chemical energy; eventually energy is transferred to the environment as heat.

cards.f: What does a food chain show?
cards.b: The transfer of energy from one organism to the next, beginning with a producer. Arrows point in the direction of energy flow.
A network of interconnected food chains.
Producer: makes its own organic nutrients by photosynthesis. Consumer: gets energy by feeding on other organisms. Decomposer: gets energy from dead or waste material.
Herbivore: eats plants. Carnivore: eats other animals.
The position of an organism in a food chain or food web (producer, primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary consumer).

cards.f: Why is energy transfer between trophic levels inefficient?
cards.b: Not all is eaten or digested (faeces); much is lost as heat from respiration and in excretory products. About 10% passes on.

cards.f: Why do food chains have fewer than five trophic levels?
cards.b: Energy is lost at each level, so too little energy remains at the top to support another population.

cards.f: Why is eating crops more energy efficient than eating livestock?
cards.b: Humans are at a lower trophic level, so there is one less transfer and less energy is lost; more people can be fed.

cards.f: Carbon cycle: processes removing and returning CO₂
cards.b: Removed: photosynthesis. Returned: respiration, decomposition, combustion. Fossil fuel formation locks carbon away.
Ecosystem: community of organisms and their environment interacting together. Biodiversity: number of different species in an area.
Housing, crop and livestock production, extraction of natural resources, freshwater and marine pollution.
Reduced biodiversity, extinction, loss of soil, flooding, increased CO₂ in the atmosphere.

cards.f: Why do species become endangered or extinct?
cards.b: Climate change, habitat destruction, hunting, overharvesting, pollution and introduced species.
Monitoring and protecting species and habitats, education, captive breeding programmes, seed banks.

short.q: Explain why only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next. [3]
short.model: Not all of an organism is eaten or digested, so some is lost in faeces, and much is used in respiration and lost as heat.
points: not all eaten / some lost in faeces
lost as heat to the environment

short.q: Explain why more people can be fed by eating crops than by eating livestock fed on crops. [3]
short.model: Eating crops removes a trophic level, so less energy is lost in respiration, heat and faeces of the animals and more energy reaches humans.

short.q: Describe the carbon cycle with reference to photosynthesis, respiration and combustion. [3]
short.model: Photosynthesis removes CO₂ from the air; respiration and combustion of fossil fuels and wood return CO₂ to the air.

short.q: Explain how deforestation can cause flooding and loss of soil. [3]
short.model: Without trees, less water is absorbed and water runs quickly into rivers causing flooding; roots no longer hold the soil, so rain washes it away.
points: fewer trees to absorb water so rapid run-off / flooding

short.q: Explain how introducing a foreign predator to a habitat could affect a food web. [3]
short.model: The new predator eats native species, reducing their populations, and the animals that feed on them lose food, so the food web is disrupted.
points: other consumers that depend on them lose food
